{{Short description|Sign representing zero or empty set}}
{{hatnote|This article is about mathematical notation. For a null unit of semiotic meaning, see [[Empty string]] or [[Zero (linguistics)]]}}
{{Other uses|Null symbol (disambiguation)|Ø (disambiguation)}}
[[File:Atheism symbol syreeni.svg|thumb|alt=∅|A null sign|class=skin-invert-image]]

The '''null sign''' (∅) is a symbol often used in [[mathematics]] for denoting the [[empty set]]. The same letter in [[linguistics]] represents [[Zero (linguistics)|zero]], the lack of an element. It is commonly used in [[phonology]], [[Morphology (linguistics)|morphology]], and [[syntax]].

==Encodings==
The symbol ∅ is available at [[Unicode]] point U+2205.<ref>[https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U2200.pdf Unicode Standard 5.2]</ref> It can be coded in [[HTML]] as {{code|&empty;}}, {{code|&#8709;}}, or {{code|&#x2205;}}. In [[LaTeX]], it can be encoded as {{code|\varnothing}} (<math>\varnothing</math>) or {{code|\emptyset}} (<math>\emptyset</math>).

==Similar letters==
Similar letters and symbols include the following:
*[[Diameter#Symbol|Diameter sign]] in [[geometry]]: {{unichar|2300|Diameter Sign}}
*[[Ø|Scandinavian letter Ø]]: majuscule {{unichar|00D8|Latin Capital Letter O with Stroke}} and minuscule {{unichar|00F8|Latin Small Letter O with Stroke}} are a part of the alphabet of [[North Germanic languages|Scandinavian languages]]. The minuscule letter is also used in the [[International Phonetic Alphabet]] (IPA) to represent [[close-mid front rounded vowel]].<ref name="Pullum & Ladusaw" />
*[[Phi|Greek letter Φ]]: majuscule {{unichar|03A6|Greek Capital Letter Phi}} and minuscule {{unichar|03C6|Greek Small Letter Phi}} are a part of the [[Greek alphabet]]. It sometimes take the form of {{unichar|03D5|Greek Phi Symbol}} and is used as a sign in different fields of studies. The {{unichar|0278|Latin Small Letter Phi}} is used in the IPA for [[voiceless bilabial fricative]].<ref name="Pullum & Ladusaw" />
*[[Theta|Greek letter Θ]]: majuscule {{unichar|0398|Greek Capital Letter Theta}} and minuscule {{unichar|03B8|Greek Small Letter Theta}} are a part of the [[Greek alphabet]]. The minuscule is used in the IPA for [[voiceless dental fricative]]. The capital letter sometimes are rendered as {{unichar|03F4|Greek Capital Theta Symbol}}.<ref name="Pullum & Ladusaw" />
*[[Oe (Cyrillic)|Cyrillic letter Ө]]: majuscule {{unichar|04E8|Cyrillic Capital Letter Barred O}} and minuscule {{unichar|04E9|Cyrillic Small Letter Barred O}} are a part of the [[Cyrillic script]]. It is used in the IPA for [[close-mid central rounded vowel]].
*[[Ef (Cyrillic)|Cyrillic letter Ф]]: majuscule {{unichar|0424|Cyrillic Capital Letter Ef}} and minuscule {{unichar|0444|Cyrillic Small Letter Ef}} are a part of the [[Cyrillic script]]. The letter took the place of [[fita]] ({{unichar|0472|Cyrillic Capital Letter Fita}} and {{unichar|0473|Cyrillic Small Letter Fita}}), a letter of [[Early Cyrillic alphabet]] in modern usages.

==Use in mathematics==
In mathematics, the '''null sign''' (∅) denotes the [[empty set]].<ref name="UCDavis">{{cite web |last1=Lankham |first1=Isaiah |last2=Nachtergaele |first2=Bruno |last3=Schilling |first3=Anne |title=Some Common Mathematical Symbols and Abbreviations (with History) |url=https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~anne/WQ2007/mat67-Common_Math_Symbols.pdf |website=University of California, Davis |access-date=2 May 2025 |page=2 |date=January 21, 2007}}</ref><ref name="Gerstein">{{cite book |last1=Gerstein |first1=Larry J. |title=Introduction to Mathematical Structures and Proofs |date=2012 |publisher=Springer |location=New York |isbn=978-1-4614-4265-3 |pages=42-43 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Introduction_to_Mathematical_Structures/qK9y768b1NQC?hl=en&gbpv=0 |access-date=2 May 2025 |via=Google Books}}</ref> Note that a [[null set]] is not necessarily an [[empty set]]. Common notations for the empty set include "{}", "∅", and "<math>\emptyset</math>". The latter two symbols were introduced by the [[Bourbaki group]] (specifically [[André Weil]]) in 1939, inspired by the letter [[Ø]] in the [[Danish orthography|Danish]] and [[Norwegian orthography|Norwegian]] alphabets<ref name="UCDavis" /> (and not related in any way to the Greek letter [[phi (letter)|Φ]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jeff560.tripod.com/set.html|title=Earliest Uses of Symbols of Set Theory and Logic|website=jeff560.tripod.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112015130/https://jeff560.tripod.com/set.html|archive-date=12 January 2012|url-status=live}}</ref>

Empty sets are used in set operations. For example:
<blockquote>
<math>A=\{2,3,5,7,11\}</math>

<math>B=\{4,6,8,9\}</math>

<math>A \cap B = ?</math>
</blockquote>

There are no common elements in the solution; so it should be denoted as:
<blockquote>
<math>A \cap B = \varnothing</math> or <math>A \cap B = \{ \}</math>
</blockquote>

==Use in linguistics==
{{See also|Zero (linguistics)|Silent letter|Null morpheme}}
In [[linguistics]], the null sign is used to indicate the absence of an element, such as a [[phoneme]] or [[morpheme]].<ref name="Pullum & Ladusaw">{{cite book |last1=Pullum |first1=Geoffrey K. |last2=Ladusaw |first2=William A. |title=Phonetic Symbol Guide |date=2013 |publisher=University of Chicago Press |isbn=978-0-226-92488-5 |pages=136-137 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Phonetic_Symbol_Guide/b7ml0qh2HMcC?hl=en&gbpv=1 |access-date=2 May 2025 |via=Google Books}}</ref>

===Morphology===
The [[English language]] was a [[fusional language]], this means the language makes use of [[Inflection|inflectional changes]] to convey multiple grammatical meanings. Although the inflectional complexity of English has been largely reduced in the course of development, the inflectional endings can be seen in earlier forms of English, such as [[Early Modern English]] (abbreviated as EModE).

The verb endings of EModE were summarised in the table below by [[Roger Lass]]:<ref>Lass, R. (1999). Phonology and Morphology. In R. Lass (Ed.), ''The Cambridge History of the English Language: 1476-1776'' (Vol. 3, pp. 137-180). Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|0-521-26476-6}}.</ref>

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;
|+ Verb Endings of EModE
|-
!  !! Present !! Past
|-
| First person singular || -∅ || -d
|-
| Second person singular || -st || -dst
|-
| Third person singular || -th, -s || -d
|}

==Use in photography==

In [[photography]] the null sign, Ø, found on [[camera lenses]] denotes the filter thread diameter, measured in millimeters. This marking indicates the size of [[Photographic filter|screw-in filters]] that can be attached to the front of the lens. This diameter is separate from any optical specification of the lens, as it is a standardized measurement for photographers to select a compatible filter. Common filter thread sizes include {{val|52|,|72|,|77|,|82|u=mm}}. If a photographer owns multiple lenses with different filter thread diameters, stepping rings can be utilized to adapt larger filters to smaller lens threads, eliminating the need to purchase duplicate filters in various sizes.{{Citation needed|date=April 2026|reason=Needs sources that clearly identify this as a null sign, and not the diameter sign ⌀}}
